instruction: Change Chrome's startup setting so it opens a new tab page instead of restoring the last session.

parameters.command: echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt update -y && echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt install jq -y

mkdir -p /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default && if [ ! -f /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default/Preferences ]; then echo '{}' > /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default/Preferences; fi && cd /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default && jq '. + {"session":{"restore_on_startup":1}}' Preferences > temp && mv temp Preferences

metadata.explanation: Task requires setting Chrome to open with a new tab page on startup. The evaluator uses the existing get_new_startup_page getter to check the Preferences file. It returns 'true' if the session.restore_on_startup value is 5 (new tab page) or if the session key doesn't exist (default behavior). Custom metric function check_startup_new_tab__bd145bbb387b98da7ba508028ec58276 compares the result against expected value 'true'.
